found: The first live run filed CairnCommons/troubles/append-door-has-no-schema-gate.json — this door validates nothing about a record's shape, so a malformed record of truth entered silently and surfaced only as a red in another component's proof.

standing: PROVED — THE APPEND DOOR HAS A SHAPE GATE. append_entry now REFUSES a record that omits `standing`, and refuses it BEFORE any file is touched — the only place a bad record of truth can be stopped, since history is append-only and cannot be edited afterwards (Law 7). found: THE GATE PAID FOR ITSELF ON ITS FIRST RUN. It refused cairn/tools/base/transitions.py::emit — the state-machine chokepoint every crossing goes through — which journaled from/to/workflow/direction and NO standing, the one field harbor_master's register reads to place a boat. Measured: zero emit-shaped records exist in any live history, so the fault had never yet become permanent. Fixed at the emitter (it is the one place that knows the crossing landed; a caller may override with a richer line, but can no longer omit it), not at every caller. Same defect class as the trouble it closes, caught while it was still cheap.
